mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of >10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and earnings momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO continues to outperform but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 70% of instances, or the positive rank IC drops below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) drop below 3.5% while payrolls (PAYEMS) growth exceeds 250k signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, reducing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% combined with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals a deflationary risk environment, lowering expected future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a concurrent surge in commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (RSAFS) above the prior six-month average by more than 8% signals a near-term acceleration in consumer spending, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when credit spreads are widening.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when consumer confidence is simultaneously rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness, which reduces household income and consumption, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in oil prices.
